name: Félinanthropie (Art Orienté Objet, 2007)
why: Marion Laval-Jeantet wore prosthetic cat paws to be accepted by a cat; no reliable media found.

name: Rebecca Allen, The Bush Soul (1997–1999)
why: Early networked VR in which the participant's 'bush soul' inhabits an animal-like avatar; no media found online.

name: Be the Bee: A Hive-to-Table Experience (National Honey Board, 2016)
why: Promotional 360° film flying as a bee; commercial.

name: Crow: The Legend (Baobab Studios, 2018)
why: Animated VR about a crow; the viewer watches rather than embodies the bird.

name: Empathy Creatures (Mélodie Mousset)
why: Venice Immersive VR where users care for a digital bird; care rather than becoming.

name: Beatriz da Costa, PigeonBlog (2006)
why: Homing pigeons carrying air-pollution sensors; animal as sensor, fits the machine/cyborg batch.

name: AKI INOMATA, Why Not Hand Over a 'Shelter' to Hermit Crabs? (2009–)
why: 3D-printed city shells for hermit crabs; aquatic, better in the water batch.

name: Sascha Pohflepp
why: Checked works with Chris Woebken (Situated Sampling Set, Elsewheres): simulation works, not animal perspective.

name: Ani Liu
why: Prix Ars Electronica 2023 honorary mention; works on reproduction and scent, no animal-perspective work found.

name: Jiabao Li, Chthulucene / Mouse Coach / ANIMO
why: Animal-themed works by Jiabao Li that are about octopus futures, a mouse coach and wildlife-aware cars rather than perceiving as an animal.

name: Texada (Josephine Anderson & Claire Sanford, NFB, IDFA DocLab 2023)
why: VR documentary on limestone and geological time; limestone guides the story but the viewer stays a human observer, so it fails the becoming rule.

name: Thinking like a mountain (Thomas Pellerey Grogan, 2021)
why: VR installation where visitors scrape and stack rocks with hand tracking; the participant handles rock rather than becoming it.

name: Stone (Shinseungback Kimyonghun, 2017) - already in global.json
why: Visitors stand inside 64 solenoids replaying waves hitting a stone on Ulleungdo to 'become the stone'; closest body-augmented rock work, but it carries no scope, so a curator must decide whether it counts as core.

name: Collective Body (Sarah Silverblatt-Buser, Venice 2025) - already in festivals.json
why: Social VR dance that assigns each participant an earth, air, water or fire avatar; the only realised XR 'becoming fire' found. It carries no scope yet.

name: Birdly Jurassic Flight (Somniacs) - already in animals-art.json
why: Prone flight simulator in which you fly as a pterosaur; the only realised XR extinct-species embodiment found. It carries no scope yet.

name: Nakayama et al., paleontological learning system (2014-2015)
why: Kinect system that animates extinct animals in sync with children's movements on a display; screen-based, not immersive XR.

name: The Dream of Zhuang Zhou (Shuai Zou et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Art Papers)
why: Multispecies VR on Zhuangzi's butterfly dream; already in hci-animal.json; belongs to insect/animal fields rather than things.

name: Mixanthropy: Holographic Metamorphic Clouds (Meichun Cai & Yiou Wang, ACM MM 2025)
why: Holographic installation with chimeras that morph in response to the viewer; the viewer watches rather than embodies.

name: Bidirectional Infection Experiences in a Virtual Environment (Tani et al., IEEE VR 2019)
why: VR with haptic vest that visualises pathogen droplets; the user stays human (infected or infecting), not the virus.

name: Texada (Josephine Anderson & Claire Sanford)
why: IDFA DocLab 2023 VR doc contrasting human and geological time through a limestone quarry; no public trailer found.

name: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies (Alchemy Immersive)
why: Venice Immersive 2023 VR180 series on the evolution of flight; shows rather than embodies.

name: Empathy Creatures
why: Venice Immersive 2025 AI-driven virtual bird that senses visitors; encounter rather than embodiment.

name: Birdly (Somniacs)
why: Full-body red-kite flight simulator shown at Sundance New Frontier, SXSW, GIFF Tous Écrans 2014 and SIGGRAPH 2014 Emerging Technologies; left to animals/HCI batches — add to sundance-new-frontier when it exists.

name: Pollinator Pathmaker: Perceptual Field (Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg)
why: Design Museum More than Human 2025 tapestry of a garden from a pollinator's perception; add to design-museum-more-than-human-2025 when animals-art writes it.

name: Tónandi (Sigur Rós & Magic Leap Studios)
why: Venice VR 2019 mixed-reality creatures that play music at your touch; interaction rather than embodiment.

name: Future Botanica (Polymorf)
why: IDFA DocLab / SXSW 2025 generative-AI plant ecosystems for future climates; design of plants, not becoming.

name: Namoo (Erick Oh)
why: Sundance 2021 animated VR in which a tree grows alongside one man's life; tree as metaphor.

name: Solwata (Felix Gaedtke & Gayatri Parameswaran)
why: Venice Immersive 2026 mixed reality on sea-level rise in the Solomon Islands; human community perspective, no nonhuman embodiment.

name: Disneynature's Wolf: an immersive experience (Silverback Films)
why: Venice Immersive 2026 Arctic wolf film; observational wildlife film.

name: Plague Inc (Ndemic Creations, 2012)
why: Strategy game where the player is a pathogen spreading across the world; map-level, not embodied.

name: Abzû (Giant Squid, 2016)
why: Underwater game with large fish schools; the player is a diver, not an animal.

name: Falcon Age (Outerloop Games, 2019)
why: VR game with a falcon companion; the player stays human.

name: Beyond Blue (E-Line Media, 2020)
why: Ocean game where the player is a human marine biologist.

name: Bird Alone (George Batchelor, 2020)
why: Mobile game about befriending a bird; the player stays human.

name: Sitting with the Other (Werner van der Zwan & Charl Linssen)
why: Named in the Augmented Noticing interview list as their chair VR work; no public source under this title. It is most likely the same project as Unconventional Self, or a paper about it.

name: Collisions (Lynette Wallworth, 2016)
why: Nyarri Morgan's Country and the Maralinga atomic tests; a human, not nonhuman, perspective, so left out.

name: Carriberrie (Dominic Allen, 2018)
why: 360° Aboriginal song and dance; watches dancers rather than embodying Country or animals.

name: Hayoun Kwon — The Bird Lady (2017)
why: VR walk through an apartment turned aviary; human viewpoint among birds.

name: Hideyuki Ando, Tomofumi Yoshida, Junji Watanabe: Save YourSelf!!! (2006)
why: Galvanic vestibular stimulation lets the wearer feel the tilt of a small figure floating in a water bowl, as if their balance lived in that object (Japan Media Arts Festival Jury Selection 2006, Ars Electronica Center 2007). Paper verified: Leonardo 46(3), 2013, doi 10.1162/leon_a_00578. No image or video found.

name: Pinta Studios (Zhang Peibin): Free Whale (Venice VR 2017)
why: Chinese VR animation about a whale; appears to show the whale rather than let the viewer become it.

name: Anicka Yi (UCCA 2025)
why: Seoul-born, New York-based artist centring machines, fungi and seaweed; relevant to more-than-human art but works are not participant-becoming and she is not East Asia-based.

name: Egun VR (Ifeoluwa 'Skodo' Osunkoya)
why: Nigerian VR prototype asking what trance possession by an Orisha deity feels like; described by IQOQO (African XR Realities Lab) but no public video or image found.

name: Patricia Domínguez — Madre Drone / Matrix Vegetal
why: Chilean artist working on plant intelligence and ethnobotany, but in HD video and installation, not XR or embodiment.

name: VJ Suave — Floresta Encantada
why: Brazilian VR installation in which visitors meet a jaguar and the pajé Txuã; shows the forest rather than making the visitor a forest being.

name: Alfredo Salazar-Caro — Dreams of the Jaguar's Daughter
why: VR trilogy on the 2018 migrant caravan; jaguar imagery but no nonhuman embodiment.

name: Navigate as a Bat (Andreasen et al., SMC 2018)
why: Real-time echolocation system in VR; Zenodo record only (no Crossref DOI), merged into the 'virtual bat' work.

name: Birdly paper (Rheiner, SIGGRAPH 2014 E-Tech)
why: DOI 10.1145/2614066.2614101 belongs to animals-art work somniacs--birdly; add it there as paper.

name: Me, the Elephant, and the Virtual World (Park, Jang, Bolter 2025)
why: VR copresence with wildlife (Eyes of the Wild); being with animals, not becoming them.

name: Kay's Sonic Torch / Sonicguide images
why: Historical photos of Leslie Kay's ultrasonic spectacles would give the 1974 work a visual.

name: Jiabao Li — Squid Map, ANIMO: WildLife Priority Mode
why: Squid Map builds a sand playground for lab squid; ANIMO proposes a wildlife-priority mode for self-driving cars. About animals, not becoming them.

name: Keiken — Liquid Perception (2026)
why: New installation on non-verbal and interspecies communication worn through a haptic heart device; first prototype October 2026, no documentation yet.

name: Anagram — Amorphous
why: Multiplayer AR/VR piece in which participants inhabit alternate-limbed bodies; still in development.

name: Jonathon Keats — Honeybee Ballet (2008), Cinema Botanica / Pornography for Plants (2007)
why: Works made for bee and plant audiences rather than letting humans become them.

name: Kuang-Yi Ku
why: Bio-design projects (Tiger Penis Project, Fellatio Modification Project, Atlas of Queer Anatomy) borrow animal traits for human bodies but are speculative objects, not perceptual works; site offline.

name: Pinar Yoldas
why: An Ecosystem of Excess imagines plastic-digesting organisms; speculative biology, not becoming.

name: Revital Cohen & Tuur Van Balen; Anicka Yi; Rachel Rossin; Ferryman Collective; Nexus Studios; Emissive
why: Checked portfolios; no work found where the participant becomes or perceives as a nonhuman.

name: Dancing with the Virtual Dervish: Virtual Bodies (Diane Gromala & Yacov Sharir, Banff 1994)
why: Banff Art and Virtual Environments piece where you enter a virtual human body; body-as-landscape, not nonhuman.

name: Archeology of a Mother Tongue (Toni Dove & Michael Mackenzie, Banff 1993)
why: Banff VR work; narrative, no nonhuman embodiment.

name: A-Volve (Sommerer & Mignonneau 1994)
why: Golden Nica 1994; visitors draw creatures that live in a water pool, but do not become them.

name: Liquid Views (Monika Fleischmann & Wolfgang Strauss 1992)
why: Narcissus mirror in virtual water; self-image dissolves in ripples, weak water-becoming.

name: Terrain 01 (Ulrike Gabriel 1993)
why: Brainwave-controlled light drives solar robots; control, not embodiment.

name: World Skin (Maurice Benayoun 1997)
why: Golden Nica CAVE work about war photography; not nonhuman.

name: Feral Robotic Dogs (Natalie Jeremijenko 2002)
why: Hacked robot dogs sniff pollutants; robot-senses work, no stable media found.

name: Zoomorph (Lisa Jevbratt)
why: Software filters showing images as various animals would see them; project page offline.

name: Humphrey (Ars Electronica Center 1994)
why: First-generation flight simulator preceding Humphrey II.

name: Finger Gloves (Rebecca Horn 1972)
why: Body extension that lengthens fingers to touch distant surfaces; no stable image found.

name: Luis Hernan — Digital Ethereal
why: Visualises and sonifies WiFi signals as spectral light paintings; project page moved, no media verified.

name: Heather Dewey-Hagborg — Stranger Visions
why: Portraits generated from found DNA; machine inference of bodies, weak fit for becoming.

name: Towards Eco-Embodiment (Kreimeier et al., ISMAR 2023)
why: VR everyday-life simulation scaled to global climate impact; no nonhuman embodiment.

name: Lichen Metaverse (Doo-Sung Yoo, Ohio State)
why: Lichen-scale virtual world; no verifiable media found.

name: Somniacs — Birdly
why: Swiss full-body flight simulator (2014) in which you fly as a red kite by flapping your arms; already in the games batch.

name: Ferryman Collective
why: Live social-VR theatre (Gumball Dreams, Tearless); no nonhuman embodiment found.

name: MLF — MEMEX | Duologue (2014)
why: Photogrammetry music-video study of a scanned human body; human-centred, not researched further.

name: MLF — U2 'Invisible' (2014)
why: Real-time visual system for a Mark Romanek music video; commercial.

name: MLF — The Measures Taken (2014)
why: Interactive light for Alexander Whitley's dance piece at the Royal Opera House; human bodies only.

name: MLF — early commercial work (McLaren P1, Vodafone Evolution of Mobile, Sony PS3 projection mapping, Intel, Famous Grouse kinetic sculpture, Saatchi NDS 2011, Just for Hits with Richard Dawkins, Liquid Light for Johnnie Walker, Ron Arad's Curtain Call)
why: Brand and event commissions 2011–2023 listed on the MLF Vimeo channel and old site; no nonhuman perspective.

name: Lichen Metaverse (Doo-Sung Yoo, Lichen Likers, Ohio State)
why: Real-time VR platform for learning from lichen symbiosis, shown in Sympoiesis 2025; no stable media found.

name: Awavena (Lynette Wallworth)
why: VR with a Yawanawa shaman in the Amazon; forest vision but not a plant perspective.

name: Giant (Milica Zec & Winslow Porter)
why: VR about a family in a war zone; human perspective, out of scope.

name: Thrive (Revolutionary Games Studio)
why: Open-source evolution game starting as a microbe; first public release year unclear (Steam 2021).

name: Jenna Sutela, From Hierarchy to Holarchy / Many-Headed (Physarum works)
why: Slime mould performances and exhibitions since 2015; artist site is JS-rendered, no media extracted.

name: The Body VR: Journey Inside a Cell
why: Educational VR at cell scale; tour rather than perspective.

name: Agar.io (Matheus Valadares, 2015)
why: Browser game where the player is a cell absorbing other cells; no official media page found.

name: FungiSync (Reality Design Lab)
why: Mixed reality mycorrhizal ritual; covered by the portfolio batch.

name: Treehugger: Wawona / Of the Oak (Marshmallow Laser Feast)
why: Tree-perspective works covered by the mlf batch.

name: Body Oracle (Danlin Huang, Ke Huang)
why: AI hieroglyphs for collective bodily poses; well documented (DOI 10.1145/3749893.3749912) but not a becoming-other work.

name: Foldiverse (Danlin Huang et al.)
why: AR paper-folding therapy game for autistic children (CHI PLAY 2024); not more-than-human; site dead.

name: TreeSense (Xin Liu, Yedan Qian)
why: Earlier listed as a portfolio work but belongs to Xin Liu / slow immediate (MIT Media Lab); left for the plants batch.

name: Coral Compass: Fighting Climate Change in Palau (Stanford VHIL, 2017)
why: 360° film about Palau's reefs; shows rather than embodies, so skipped.

name: Our Blue Planet VR (BBC Earth)
why: 3D 360° dives with manta rays and octopuses; nature documentary without embodiment.

name: Feed and Grow: Fish (2016)
why: Indie game where the player is a fish that grows by eating others; developer not verified.

name: Adventure: Ice Dive / Submerged (Apple Immersive, 2024)
why: Apple Vision Pro immersive films underwater and under ice, shown at Venice Immersive 2025; human protagonists.

name: Doug Aitken — Underwater Pavilions (2016)
why: Mirrored sculptures moored underwater off Catalina Island that divers swim through; no official video found.

name: Seeds not found: Becoming Coral, Hydrocosm, We Are Ocean, In the Belly of the Whale, Vertical Oceans, Whale VR
why: Searched on YouTube and the web without finding a verifiable XR work under these titles. (Breathe is Diego Galafassi's Sundance 2020 work, covered by the festivals batch.)
